chapters.title: Chapter 5: Filing Your Return Step by Step

lessons.title: Filing ITR-1 Online: A Walkthrough on the Income Tax Portal

body.text: The portal will happily let you submit a wrong return in fifteen minutes. This walkthrough is designed to slow you down at exactly the five moments where a careless click costs money.

children.text: You have your documents ready from Chapter 2, you know your income from Chapter 3, and you have picked ITR-1 in Chapter 4. Now you file. This lesson follows the actual screens of the e-filing portal for AY 2026-27, in five stages: starting the return, validating the sections, paying any balance, submitting, and verifying.

columns.label: Online Mode (Recommended for ITR-1)
points: Filed entirely in your browser on incometax.gov.in
Data pre-filled from your profile, Form 16 data, Form 26AS and AIS
Tax computed live as you edit
Pay balance tax and e-verify in the same flow

columns.label: Offline Utility
points: You download a pre-filled JSON file and import it into the utility
Useful for long returns with many schedules, worked on over several sittings
The finished return is exported as a JSON file and uploaded to the portal
More common for ITR-2 and ITR-3 filers and tax professionals

stats.label: Tab 2
stats.context: To tick off every TDS entry

stats.label: Tab 3
stats.context: To catch interest, dividends and gains

stats.label: Tab 4
stats.context: For savings interest and tax payment

cells: Dashboard
Click e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then File Income Tax Return
Only start from incometax.gov.in, never from a link in an SMS or email
Assessment year and mode
Select Assessment Year 2026-27 and Online, then Continue
AY 2026-27 is for income earned in FY 2025-26. Picking the wrong year files a return for the wrong period
Pending return
Choose Resume Filing to continue a saved draft, or Start New Filing to begin again
Start New Filing discards your saved draft
Status
Select Individual and Proceed
HUF is a different taxpayer with its own PAN
ITR form
Select ITR-1 from the dropdown, Proceed, note the documents listed, then Let's Get Started
If you later find income that ITR-1 cannot hold, go back and start again with the right form
Reason for filing
Tick the reason that applies, such as taxable income above the basic exemption limit, or a high-value transaction condition
If you are filing only because of a trigger like foreign travel or electricity spend, select that reason rather than a generic one
Tax regime
Answer 'If you want to opt out of New Tax Regime'. No is pre-selected
Select Yes only if you have worked out that the old regime is better, and only if you are filing by the due date

body.title: The Button That Deletes Your Work
body.question: Meenal, a teacher in Nagpur, filled in half her ITR-1 yesterday and closed the browser. Today, when the portal asks about her pending return, she clicks Start New Filing to 'refresh' the form. What happens?
options: The portal reloads her draft with updated AIS data
Her saved draft is discarded and she starts again from the beginning
Two returns are created and she can submit either one
Nothing, since drafts are always kept until the due date
body.explanation: Start New Filing discards the pending draft. To continue where she left off, she should click Resume Filing. If she does want fresh pre-filled data, for example because a late TDS entry has now appeared in 26AS, starting again is reasonable, but she should note her earlier edits first.

children.text: The return opens on a summary page listing Personal Information, Gross Total Income, Total Deductions, Tax Paid and Total Tax Liability. Open each, review the pre-filled data, edit where needed, and click Confirm at the end. The first four must be confirmed before you can move ahead. Open the drills below as you reach each section.

body.title: Drill: Personal Information and Gross Total Income

content.caption: What to Click and What to Change

cells: Personal Information: profile and contact
Name, address, mobile and email; secondary contact details are now allowed
Update an old address or add a secondary email
Personal Information: bank accounts
All accounts held during the year, and one pre-validated account nominated for refund
Add a savings account opened during the year; untick a closed account as the refund account
Gross Total Income: salary
Salary pre-filled from employers' TDS data
Add the second employer's salary if you switched jobs; claim exempt allowances only from the listed options
Gross Total Income: house property
Self-occupied or let out, rent, municipal tax, interest
Add your second property; enter the tenant's PAN or TAN if they deducted TDS on rent
Gross Total Income: other sources
Savings interest, deposit interest, dividends, interest on refund, family pension
Add savings interest from every bank, even with no TDS
Gross Total Income: Section 112A
Long-term equity gains up to ₹1.25 lakh
Enter the gain from your mutual fund capital gains statement

body.title: Drill: Total Deductions, Tax Paid and Total Tax Liability

content.caption: What to Click and What to Change

cells: Total Deductions
Deductions allowed in your chosen regime, each with its required details
Add the 80D policy for your parents that you never declared to HR; remove deductions not allowed in the new regime
Tax Paid: TDS on salary
One entry per employer, matching Form 26AS
Rarely edited; if an employer's TDS is missing, contact the employer rather than typing it in
Tax Paid: TDS other than salary and TCS
Bank, tenant, dividend and property TDS; TCS on foreign travel or remittances
Make sure the income behind every TDS entry has been reported
Tax Paid: advance and self-assessment tax
Challans you paid yourself
Add a challan paid outside the filing flow using its BSR code, challan number and date
Total Tax Liability
Tax, rebate, cess, interest, fee, and the final payable or refund
No direct edits. If the result looks wrong, go back to the section causing it

body.text: Pre-filled does not mean verified. If you change a pre-filled figure, for example reducing interest because AIS shows a joint FD at its full value, first submit feedback on AIS and keep a note of the reason. The department compares your return with AIS, and differences you cannot explain are the usual trigger for a notice.

markDefs.definition: Tax you pay yourself, after the year ends and before filing, to cover the gap between your final tax liability plus interest and the TDS, TCS and advance tax already paid.

children.text: If the Total Tax Liability section shows tax payable, you must clear it as

before your return is complete. The portal offers Pay Now and Pay Later. Pay Now takes you to the e-Pay Tax service, and once the payment succeeds the challan details flow into your Tax Paid section automatically. A return filed without paying the tax and interest due can be treated as defective, so Pay Later is only a way to step away, not a way to skip payment.

body.caption: Choosing the Right Challan Head in e-Pay Tax (Major Head 0021: Income Tax Other Than Companies)

cells: Advance tax, paid during the year
Self-assessment tax, paid before filing
Tax on regular assessment, paid against a demand

body.title: Pick the Minor Head
body.textWithBlank: When paying the balance tax on your return before filing, you select Major Head 0021 and Minor Head ___.
body.explanation: Minor Head 300 is self-assessment tax. Choosing 100, advance tax, by mistake is a common error. The money still reaches the department against your PAN, but it will not appear where the return expects it, and correcting the head later takes a separate request.

body.title: How Much Goes on the Challan?
body.prompt: Anand's Total Tax Liability section shows total tax, including cess, of ₹84,300. His Tax Paid section shows TDS of ₹71,800. The portal has also computed ₹1,250 of interest for not paying advance tax. How much should his self-assessment tax challan be for?
body.explanation: Tax still due is ₹84,300 − ₹71,800 = ₹12,500. Self-assessment tax must also cover interest, so he pays ₹12,500 + ₹1,250 = ₹13,750. If he paid only ₹12,500, the portal would still show a balance. The next lesson explains how that interest is calculated.

body.label: Paid Outside the Filing Flow?
body.value: BSR code, challan serial number, date
body.context: If you paid self-assessment tax separately, enter these three details from your challan receipt in the Tax Paid section so the payment is credited to this return.

children.text: On the Preview and Submit Your Return page, tick the declaration and click Proceed to Validation. The portal checks the return for errors. If it lists any, go back and fix each one; you cannot move on until the list is clear. Then click Preview to see the complete return as the department will receive it, and read it end to end before clicking Proceed to Verification.

body.caption: Common Reasons Returns Fail Validation or Draw Questions Later

cells: TDS claimed on FD interest or rent, but the income itself was not reported
Report the income under the right head
No pre-validated bank account selected for refund
Pre-validate an account under My Profile and select it
Deduction entered without required details, such as a policy number
Complete every field the dropdown asks for
Tax payable shown but no self-assessment tax paid
Pay the balance through e-Pay Tax and let the challan flow in
Old regime selected in a return filed after the due date
Only the new regime is available in a belated return

children.text: After submission the portal offers three choices: e-Verify Now, the recommended option; e-Verify Later, within 30 days of filing; and Verify via ITR-V, which means printing, signing and posting the acknowledgement to the Centralized Processing Centre in Bengaluru within 30 days. A return that is not verified in time is treated as never filed. Lesson 3 of this chapter walks through each verification method.

body.text: Once verified, download your acknowledgement from e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then View Filed Returns, and save it in your FY 2025-26 folder. This is the ITR acknowledgement that banks, lenders and visa offices ask for.

body.title: Shruti Files on 29 July
body.scenario: Shruti, 26, is a first-time filer working at an IT services firm in Indore. On 29 July 2026 she logs in to file ITR-1. The pre-filled salary matches her Form 16. Other sources shows FD interest from AIS but no savings interest. Her Tax Paid section shows salary TDS and TDS on her FD. The Total Tax Liability section shows ₹6,200 payable. She is tempted to click Pay Later, submit, choose e-Verify Later, and deal with it all next week.
body.prompt: Walk Shruti through what she should do at each remaining stage, and explain what could go wrong with her plan.
body.modelAnswer: Stage 2: before confirming Gross Total Income, she should add savings interest from every bank account, since AIS shows it and no TDS does not mean no tax. This may increase the tax payable slightly, so she should recheck the figure. Stage 3: she should click Pay Now and pay the full balance, including any interest shown, through e-Pay Tax under Minor Head 300, so the challan flows into Tax Paid automatically. If she clicks Pay Later and submits without paying, the return can be treated as defective, and interest keeps running on the unpaid tax. With the due date only two days away, she has no time to sort this out later. Stage 4: tick the declaration, Proceed to Validation, fix any errors, preview the full return and read it. Stage 5: choose e-Verify Now with an Aadhaar OTP. e-Verify Later is allowed within 30 days, but first-time filers often forget, and an unverified return is treated as never filed, which would leave her with a late return, a late fee and the new regime as her only option. Finally, she should download the acknowledgement.

body.title: Final Check Before You Click Submit
steps: Assessment Year shows 2026-27 and the form is ITR-1
Reason for filing and tax regime are correct
Salary from every employer is included
All savings interest, FD interest and dividends are reported, even without TDS
Every TDS entry has its matching income reported
A pre-validated bank account is selected for the refund
Any balance tax and interest is paid, and the challan shows in Tax Paid
You have read the full preview
You are ready to e-verify immediately

points: Start from e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then File Income Tax Return, and select Assessment Year 2026-27 and Online mode for ITR-1
Resume Filing keeps your draft; Start New Filing discards it
Tick the correct reason for filing and answer the regime question carefully; opting out of the new regime works only in a return filed by the due date
Review and Confirm each of the five sections, editing pre-filled data where it is incomplete and noting the reason for any change
Pay any balance as self-assessment tax under Major Head 0021 and Minor Head 300 before submitting, since unpaid tax can make the return defective
Proceed to Validation, fix errors, read the preview, then e-verify within 30 days, ideally immediately, and download the acknowledgement

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. Screen names, button labels and the order of steps reflect the e-filing portal for AY 2026-27 at the time of writing and are updated by the Income Tax Department from time to time. Follow the current on-screen instructions and the official user manuals, or consult a qualified tax professional.
